## Implemented wiring

`build_ports` connects the ETABS profile, role manager, guard, lock, identity store, opener, revision snapshots, preflight and run basis to the engine ports. Both CSI ports share the written-item book and a tolerance provider from the immutable run header. Missing or nonnumeric tolerance stays unavailable. The builder refuses command-line tool entries as H-G8 and `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` maps to exit 2. Real synthetic-server processes cover the cycle, server preflight, units, bound and unbound previews, and revision wiring.

The binder reads the existing model identity without resolving the file path, preserving the next model-state read's outside-edit detection. Hand-wired adapters keep binder-provided pre-images by default. Production takes the pre-image before ledgering a reconcilable write. A new open can be previewed without a binding. A stale bound open takes the normal refusal path. A resumed port never claims launch ownership.

## Blocker and implementation scope requested

The fixture launches one fake host and starts the edit-cycle workflow with `copy_on_open=True`. Both `m` and `m@copy` bind to PID 4242. At cuts after the original open, its completed step is still journaled as effect `write`, action `open`. The persisted fake host shows the working-copy path, and the bindings show the original and copy on the same instance. The failed resume asks `engine.host_state` about `m` being unloaded and offers only `abandon`. It is the expected adapter layout, not fake PID loss. The fixture rejects that unexpected request.

Spec 0007 §4.5 Step 2 says that the working copy opens in the same host instance and that the original is not read again afterward. It also says this initial open writes no model content. Spec 0001 §4.7 EC1 journals the completed post-open working copy and directs subsequent calls to it. Spec 0001 §§4.5.1 and 4.5.4 describe recovery for models the run wrote. The initial opener nevertheless enters that set through `Fold.written()`.

A second failure of EC1 is present in the successful open-cut journal. The open marks `m` dirty and the final `~end.check_model.m` reads the active copy under the original label via their shared instance. The same-process timeout path is also incomplete. When an open's outcome is immediately resolved as `applied`, `_ctx_impl` marks it and returns without the post-open binding or EC1 copy.

The owner approved explicit conservative tool metadata. B-562 owns the reviewed documents amendment. The implementation scope additions below are all under `packages/eng-harness/`.

The expected original absence requires a specific open attempt marked true that completed with a result or reconciled `applied`. Its `~post.working_copy.<key>` is the latest applicable completed working-copy step and began after the open closed. Its source key matches and the returned copy key is distinct. The historical `model_saved` at that path names that copy and has role `working_copy`. It occurs between the copy step's start and completion. A later revision can supersede that historical role. A stale result, restore/rerun, later contradictory source binding, another actual original write, or a pending source open keeps the safety check. Readiness and model-content comparisons for actual writes to the copy stay in force.

The existing T19a cycle and matrix are already scoped. Assert original bind and units before a still-live post-copy, no original content check after the copy, working-copy checks after actual writes, one effect-write attempt per cut, and no engine decision inferred for unknown long operations. Preserve lower-level unit checks and leases across restarts. An unreadable or absent original remains a loss for actual writes. A newer flagged open can never clear an existing dirty flag. `_tools.py`, the snapshot registry, and the write ledger need no new capability or persistent data.

The existing resume flow excludes operations for lost or reopened model keys before reconciliation. The initial source-open cut has no earlier binding, so its real test reaches `engine.in_flight`. Review the already-bound, lost-key edge independently. A content-free action still requires its real journaled outcome, and an absent model permits no automatic evidence or read-back from a different host model. The approved docs should state any special handling needed for that edge before source changes.

B-562 should specify the port capability and journal payload in spec 0001 §§4.4.2 and 4.8 and its effect on §4.5.4 and invariant 1. EC1 should cover immediate `applied` and replay completing the original binding/units before a still-live copy. Cite spec 0007 §4.5 Step 2 and spec 0002 §4.5.9 for the CSI override. `Fold.writes` remains the source for effect-write recovery rules and restore cuts. No engine, journal or public port source was edited in this session.
